page.overview:
Who is Gyatso?

A powerful and wise airbender, Gyatso was well known for his kindness and sense of humor. As a result, he became an advisor to others from his early years, greatly influencing Roku's diplomatic and open-minded trajectory as the Avatar and the Air Nomads' growing efforts to help the needy across the world. In his elder years, he became a leading figure at the Southern Air Temple and imparted his philosophy to his pupil Aang. Though Aang learned airbending under him as part of his Avatar training, the monk always allowed time for fun and games.

Gyatso was slain during the genocide of the Air Nomads, during which Fire Lord Sozin invaded the air temples. The place where his body was found revealed that he had managed to defeat many comet-enhanced Fire Nation soldiers before his demise.

Born around the early 70s BG, He also met his sky bison companion, a female named Lola, at the air temple. From an early point, Gyatso became known for his sense of humor, particularly his tendency to attack others with his self-baked fruit pies. As he grew older, he proved to be a highly capable airbender and seemingly destined to reach master status at a young age.

Everything changed in 67 BG, when Yama died on a relief mission in the Earth Kingdom when an entire village was swallowed by a massive sinkhole caused by reckless mining of the Western Kingdom Trading Company. Gyatso felt great anger over this event, wishing that he could have saved his sister as well as cursing the company for their misconduct and the Council of Elders for their inaction over the tragedy. Unable to move forward due to the grief he held over his sister's death, he suffered from a mental block that affected his ability to perform airbending consistently; instead, he was only able to airbend in certain emotional situations. The decline of his bending abilities further demotivated Gyatso, and arrested the progress of his training. His relationship with Lola also suffered due to his grief, as the sky bison sensed his internal turmoil.
